label.en: Statutory monthly gross minimum wage, no FYA implemented

description.en: $MinWage is the French statutory gross monthly minimum wage (SMIC brut mensuel, based on the standard legal working time), with a latest modelled value of €1,801.80/month (no adjustment for a reduced first-year-of-activity rate is applied, per the modeller's comment). In the EUROMOD France spine it is used in ConstDef_fr's DefConst function to build the derived constant $mc_yem_max, part of a set of constants supporting the COVID-19 wage-compensation schemes, and it is also used as the Comp_Cond (compensation/eligibility condition) parameter in tscse_fr's BenCalc function, which computes the family-related social-insurance-contribution ('SIC') component. The FR benefits note does not quote the SMIC monthly figure directly but repeatedly uses SMIC as the reference wage for eligibility ceilings (e.g. child-earnings tests expressed as a share of SMIC), consistent with this constant's role as the general minimum-wage reference used across benefit rules.

description.en: $Minwage_hourly is the hourly value of the French statutory minimum wage (SMIC horaire), latest modelled value €11.88, labelled by the modeller as covering the 2021-2024 period. Its 2025/26 annual value of 47,100 EUR is internally consistent with the monthly PSS of 3,925 EUR used to build the $tsc_group1_lim/$tsc_groupA_lim complementary-pension income limits (1x monthly PSS).

label.en: qualifying period for bhl: over last 12 months

description.en: This constant defines a qualifying-condition threshold (value 4) that must be met within a rolling 12-month reference period for an insured person to qualify for the Social-Security-paid sickness daily allowance (indemnités journalières) simulated by the sickcomp_fr policy. It is passed as the Comp_Cond condition parameter of the BenCalc function documented as computing the 'number of days paid by Social Security', i.e. it gates whether sickness compensation days are paid at all. It belongs to the general qualifying-period rules of the French sickness insurance scheme, alongside the parallel 3-month condition ($bhl_Qper3) for employees and the 12-month condition for self-employed/farmers ($bhl_Qper12_se); the theme note on French benefits does not cover this sick-pay scheme, so the precise legal threshold this '4' represents (e.g. months of contribution) could not be confirmed from the sources.

It feeds the Elig_Cond parameter of the Elig function documented as testing 'basic eligibility for the scheme - farmers', i.e. it determines whether a farmer/self-employed individual's recent affiliation or contribution record is sufficient to pass the initial eligibility test (it is referenced at three sites, reflecting reuse of this threshold across related eligibility checks). It corresponds to the qualifying-period condition of the farmers' (MSA) and self-employed sickness insurance branch, contrasting with the shorter 3-month condition ($bhl_Qper3) applicable to ordinary employees; the theme note on French benefits does not describe this scheme, so the description relies on the constant's name, label and usage.

description.en: This constant is the daily ceiling (maximum) on the maternity, paternity, and adoption leave benefit paid to an eligible parent, expressed as a currency amount per day. In the EUROMOD spine it is used in policy bmact_fr's BenCalc function as the Comp_UpLim parameter, capping the daily compensation computed for the eligible parent, and again in bpact_fr's ArithOp function as the UpLim parameter when computing the final daily benefit amount. These leave benefits are daily cash allowances (indemnités journalières) paid under the French social security/health insurance scheme to replace earnings during maternity, paternity, or adoption leave, and like other daily social-security allowances they are subject to a statutory daily cap; the theme documentation available for this batch does not itself describe the maternity/paternity leave scheme, so this account relies on the constant's name, label and usage.

This reflects the French social-security practice of setting statutory minimum daily allowances for sickness, maternity, paternity and disability-related income replacement; the theme documentation supplied for this batch does not itself cover this specific minimum, so the description is derived from the constant's name, label and its usage sites.

label.en: Amount for children with one parent -FYA

description.en: This constant is the monthly amount (2025/2026 value 200.18 euros, gross of CRDS) of the French Family Support Allowance (Allocation de soutien familial, ASF) paid per dependent child who lives with a lone parent (i.e. one parent is deceased, has abandoned the child, or fails to pay maintenance). In the EUROMOD spine it is used in policy bchor_fr's BenCalc function as the Comp_perElig parameter, i.e. the per-child amount that is multiplied by the number of eligible children to compute the benefit. The ASF is not means-tested, is not subject to income tax, but is subject to CRDS; in the EUROMOD model it is simulated only for children of widows/widowers because abandonment or non-payment of alimony cannot be identified in the data. The 2022 mid-year increases (July and November 2022, when support for single-parent families was raised as a government priority) are incorporated via a weighted-average value in the model's yearly amount.

In the EUROMOD spine it is used in policy bchor_fr's BenCalc function as the Comp_perElig parameter, the per-eligible-child amount multiplied by the number of qualifying children to compute the benefit payable. Like the lone-parent ASF amount, this benefit is not means-tested and is exempt from income tax but subject to CRDS; because EUROMOD data cannot identify children whose both parents are deceased or have abandoned them, the benefit is in practice simulated only for children of widows/widowers, with the 2022 mid-year rate increases reflected through a weighted-average value.

It is used in tscer_fr's BenCalc function (Comp_UpLim parameter, 'Calculate applicable reduction coefficient') as the cap applied in the formula (coefficient/0.6)*[1.6*(annual SMIC/annual gross income subject to social contributions) - 1], which is maximal at the SMIC (minimum wage) and phases out for incomes above 1.6 times the SMIC. The reduction applies to sickness, family benefits, housing (FNAL), CSA, old-age, complementary pension and unemployment contributions.

label.en: Additional contribution

description.en: This constant holds the rate of the "additional contribution" (contribution additionnelle), one of several social-levy components historically applied to capital and investment income (e.g. property income, interest, dividends) in France, in addition to CSG and CRDS. It is used in the tsckt_fr policy's ArithOp function (commented "Liability") to compute the total social-contribution liability due on capital income. Per Table 2.69 of the EUROMOD France Country Report, the additional contribution stood at 0.30% in 2017-2018, when it formed part of a 6.80% combined rate (with the social and solidarity contributions) that brought the overall levy including CSG and CRDS to 15.5%-17.2%; from 2019 it was abolished and folded into the unified "solidarity levy", consistent with only 2 recorded values since 2006 and a latest value of n/a.

Per Table 2.69 of the EUROMOD France Country Report, this rate was 4.50% in 2017 and 2018, contributing to a combined 6.80% total (and to a 15.5%/17.2% total once CSG and CRDS were included); it was discontinued from 2019 when merged into the single "solidarity levy", which is reflected in the parameter's latest value being n/a and 5 recorded values dating back to 2006.

According to Table 2.69 of the EUROMOD France Country Report, it was set at 2.00% in 2017-2018 as part of the 6.80% combined capital-income social-contribution rate, and was abolished from 2019 when it was absorbed into the new unified "solidarity levy" of 7.5%; this matches the constant's 4 recorded values since 2006 and its latest value of n/a.

It is used in the tsckt_fr policy's ArithOp function (commented "Liability") to compute the social-contribution liability on capital income. Per Table 2.69 of the EUROMOD France Country Report, the rate is 7.5% for 2019-2025 (its latest recorded value, matching the 0.075 stored here), which together with CSG and CRDS brings the total social levy on capital income to 17.2%.

label.en: CSG reduction threshold

description.en: This is the annual earnings threshold, computed as four times the PSS (Plafond de la Sécurité Sociale, the French social-security earnings ceiling), above which the 1.75% professional-expenses reduction no longer applies to the CSG (Contribution Sociale Généralisée) base — above this level the CSG is calculated on 100% of gross earnings instead of 98.25%. It is used in policy tinty_fr (personal income tax module) in the ArithOp computing the 'Amount of CSG - earnings' and the BenCalc computing 'Amount of CSG - unemployment benefits', and equivalently in the CSG policy tscxc_fr for the same two computations, always as a formula input alongside $csg_redrate. Per the taxes documentation, CSG is levied on 98.25% of current gross earnings until this four-times-PSS threshold, and on 100% above it.

It is used across several social-contribution and tax modules: in bsa00_fr to calculate family work income, in tinty_fr and tscxc_fr to compute the amount of CSG on earnings and on unemployment benefits, and in tscdf_fr to compute a contribution liability. The taxes documentation states the CSG base is gross income after a 1.75% reduction for professional expenses (applied to employment income and unemployment benefit but not to capital income or sickness benefits).

label.en: First income limit for singles

description.en: Income threshold of EUR 250,000 marking the start of the taxable band for single taxpayers under the Contribution Exceptionnelle sur les Hauts Revenus (CEHR), France's exceptional tax on high earners in place since 2013. In tin_fr's SchedCalc function it is used as the Band_UpLim of the first tax band (comment: 'Exceptional contributions on high income earners: singles'), i.e. the upper limit of the band taxed at 0% and the point above which the 3% rate starts to apply on the reference tax income (RFR, personal income tax base plus taxable capital income). It is also used in tinto01_fr's Elig function as the eligibility condition for single taxpayers under the related Contribution Différentielle sur les Hauts Revenus (CDHR), a 2025 one-year (subsequently renewed) top-up levy that also applies from EUR 250,000 RFR for singles.

label.en: Maximum tax credit for child care expenses

description.en: This constant is the annual per-child ceiling (EUR 3,500) applied to eligible child-care expenses for the French personal income tax (IRPP) child-care tax credit. In the model it is used in policy tintcot_fr, function BenCalc with parameter Comp_perElig (func_comment 'Tax credit on child care expenses'), where it caps the amount of expenditure on which the credit is computed on a per-eligible-child basis. Per the taxes theme note and the EUROMOD Country Report, households that pay someone to look after a child can deduct 50% of the amount paid, up to this EUR 3,500-per-child annual ceiling; the credit is non-refundable and cannot be combined with other child-care deductions.

label.en: Increase for dependent children

description.en: Sets the flat-rate increase added to the Prime Pour l'Emploi (PPE) employment-bonus tax credit for dependent children. It is used in the tintcee_fr policy's BenCalc function as a Comp_perTU value (func_comment 'PPE: Amount corresponding to full time: lone parents'), meaning it is added once to the tax unit's PPE amount when the associated eligibility condition (dependent children present) is satisfied. The PPE was a refundable tax credit designed to encourage return to/retention of employment via the personal income tax (IRPP) system; it was abolished on 31 December 2015 and replaced from 1 January 2016 by the Prime d'Activité (integrated into the RSA/Activity Allowance framework), which is why this constant has no value from 2016 onward.

label.en: Benefit amount per month: basic

description.en: This is the monthly ceiling (maximum) amount of the AAH (Allocation aux adultes handicapés), France's means-tested disability benefit, paid to disabled adults with a permanent disability of at least 80%, or 50-80% combined with recognised unemployability. AAH is a differential benefit computed as (income threshold - income)/12, and this constant supplies the upper limit of that calculation in bdi_fr/BenCalc via the Comp_UpLim parameter, i.e. the cap a recipient can receive when their income is zero. The value of 1033.32 EUR/month matches the 2025 maximum monthly AAH amount reported in the Country Report (Table 2.24) and the policy-description note; the amount is uprated annually and, for years with mid-year increases (e.g. 2022), the modelled figure is a weighted average of the pre- and post-increase amounts via the FYA mechanism.

label.en: Benefit amount: supplement for independent living

description.en: This constant is the flat-rate monthly supplement for independent living ('Majoration pour la vie autonome'), an add-on to AAH for disabled recipients who receive the benefit at the full rate (or as a complement to an old-age/invalidity pension) and who do not work. It is used in bdi_fr/BenCalc as the comp_perTU parameter, labelled 'Supplement for independent living', added on top of the basic AAH amount for eligible recipients. The value 104.77 EUR/month matches Table 2.25 of the Country Report; in the EUROMOD model this supplement is simulated for individuals receiving AAH at the full rate as well as those reporting zero earnings, and recipients eligible for both this supplement and the (unmodelled) disability supplement must choose one or the other.

label.en: Means test: income disregard for non-disabled partner

description.en: This parameter is a flat-rate annual deduction applied to the income of a non-AAH-recipient partner when computing the AAH means test for a disabled person living as a couple, used in bdi_fr/BenCalc via the Comp_perElig parameter ('Disregard of income of non-disabled head or partner'). Per the Country Report (Table 2.23), from January 2022 to September 2023 a 5,000 EUR annual disregard was applied to the partner's earned income (not capital income) before it was counted toward the AAH income test. Since 1 October 2023 the partner's income is generally excluded from the AAH eligibility test altogether (except under the more-advantageous 'conjugalisation' rule), which is why the latest modelled value of this constant is n/a — the disregard mechanism it fed became largely obsolete after the reform.

description.en: This is the annual income threshold used in the AAH means test for a single (non-couple) claimant, used in bdi_fr/BenCalc as the Comp_perElig eligibility parameter, whose function comment notes it applies as the income limit since 2024 (following the reform under which, from October 2023, only the single-person threshold is generally used in the eligibility test). label.en: Income test: minimum threshold to be considered an earner

description.en: This is the minimum annual income (assessed on n-2 income, i.e. income from two years before the benefit year) that a partner must earn to be classed as an 'earner' for the means test of the PAJE base allowance (Allocation de base) and a related PAJE-family benefit computed in policy bchlg_fr (e.g. the means-tested birth grant, which the policy note says shares the same income thresholds as PAJE base). It is used in bchyc_fr's Elig function to decide whether a couple counts as a 'one-earner' or 'two-earner' couple - which determines which income-ceiling schedule applies - and in bchlg_fr's BenCalc to count the number of earning partners in the tax unit for the same test. The 2025/2026 policy note states this earner threshold is €5,983 (n-2 income), matching the constant's latest value.

description.en: This constant sets the monthly amount (€749.18 as the latest value, since 2006) of the increased 'PreParE Majorée' rate of the French child-rearing benefit (Complément de Libre Choix d'Activité, CLCA, now called Prestation partagée d'éducation de l'enfant, PreParE), which is paid to families with at least three children who fully stop working to care for a young child and who are also receiving PAJE's basic young-child allowance (referred to in the model as PAJE-FYA). It is used in the bchcc_fr policy's BenCalc function as the Comp_perTU parameter (function comment 'PreParE Majorée: amount'), which computes the per-tax-unit monthly benefit amount for this majorée case. PAJE-PreParE is a family benefit that supports parents who reduce or stop working to care for a child under 3, and the theme documentation notes a 'PreParE Majorée' option specifically available for families with three or more children.

The 2025/2026 taxes theme note does not cover this tax because it was abolished from 2018 and replaced by the real-estate wealth tax (modelled separately as trewl_fr/IFI), so this parameter is only relevant to pre-2018 EUROMOD systems.

description.en: This is P0forf, the fixed monthly floor amount used in the French housing benefit (Allocation Logement / APL, policy bhotn_fr) to compute P0, the minimum-participation floor: P0 = Max(P0forf, 8.5%*(L+C)), where L is the eligible rent and C the lump-sum charge. Per the Country Report (Table 2.39) P0forf rises each year (e.g. 35.39 in 2022 to 39.56 in Oct 2025); the stored value here is expressed as a mid-year weighted average via the EUROMOD FYA (from-year-average) mechanism.

description.en: This is the 'Rent Baseline' amount for a single person, used in the French Housing Benefit (Allocation Logement, APL/AL, policy bhotn_fr) to compute the Personal Participation rate. In bhotn_fr/BenCalc (Comp_perTU, 'Baseline rent, part of Tl') it forms the denominator of RL = L / Rent Baseline (country report Table 2.41 and Equation 6), where L is the household's ceiling rent. RL is then converted via a banded schedule (Table 2.42) into Tl, which together with Tf makes up the personal participation rate Tp = Tf + Tl used in Pp = P0 + Tp*Rp (minimal personal participation, deducted from the benefit). The value is a within-year weighted average reflecting the uprating that occurred in July 2022 and October 2023.

label.en: Income limit for single person- FYA

description.en: This constant is the monthly maximum income (resource) ceiling used to compute the Solidarity Allowance for the Elderly (Allocation de solidarité aux personnes âgées, ASPA) for a single person, set at €1034.28/month for 2025. In the bsaoa_fr policy it feeds the BenCalc function's Comp_perTU parameter, which calculates the differential benefit as this maximum amount minus the household's quarterly net taxable income (plus AAH, but excluding family and housing benefits) divided by three; the result is the ASPA payment, floored at zero if negative. ASPA is a means-tested top-up for persons aged 65 and over who are retired and have limited resources, replacing the former 'minimum vieillesse', and this single-person ceiling is one of the two family-situation-dependent thresholds (single vs couple) reported in the Country Report's Table 2.35.

classification.reason: Income limit for single person benefit

label.en: Income limit for couples - FYA

description.en: This constant is the monthly maximum income (resource) ceiling used to compute the Solidarity Allowance for the Elderly (ASPA) for a couple, set at €1605.73/month for 2025; it applies when at least one member of the couple is aged 65 or over. In the bsaoa_fr policy it is used by the BenCalc function's Comp_perTU parameter to calculate the differential ASPA benefit as this couple ceiling minus the couple's combined quarterly net taxable income (plus AAH, excluding family and housing benefits) divided by three, with the payment floored at zero if the result is negative. ASPA is the means-tested minimum-resources benefit for elderly, retired persons with limited income, and this couple threshold is the higher of the two family-situation amounts shown in Table 2.35 of the Country Report.

description.en: This constant sets the flat rate of the CRDS (Contribution pour le Remboursement de la Dette Sociale, the social security debt repayment contribution), equal to 0.5% (0.005) and unchanged since 2006-01-01 according to the model's value history. In the EUROMOD policy tscdf_fr, it is used in the ArithOp function computing the CRDS 'Liability' (tax base multiplied by this rate), and it is also referenced in the ArithOp function of bsa00_fr that calculates family work income, presumably to net out the CRDS deduction. Per the Country Report, CRDS is levied at the same uniform 0.5% rate across all income categories it applies to (employment, self-employment, pension, unemployment/activity-allowance income, family benefits, capital income, housing benefits, and sickness daily allowances), applied on the same broad basis as CSG (i.e., gross income after the standard abatement), and is not deductible for tax purposes.

It is used in bsa00_fr/BenCalc via the comp_perElig parameter, which adds this per-eligible-child amount on top of the base household maximum when computing the RSA entitlement. The Country Report notes that before 2009 the API was a separate benefit paid on top of only one other allowance and so is not separately simulated in EUROMOD; the value (EUR 276.73/month in 2025) matches the France country report's Table 2.28 rate for 'Lone parent with children under 3 – each child after the 2nd'.

label.en: Rate for calculation of maximum amount of individual bonus

description.en: Percentage rate (29.101%) applied to the activity-allowance lump sum (montant forfaitaire, $bsawk_minamt) to determine the maximum monthly amount of the individual work bonus ("bonification individuelle") within the Activity Allowance (Prime d'activité, RSA-activité/PPE successor). It is used in bsawk_fr's ArithOp "Calculate bonus in the activity allowance" formula, together with $bsawk_minamt, to compute the bonus payable to each working household member whose individual work income lies between 0.5 and 1.5 times the SMIC (net). Per the Country Report, this rate replaced the earlier 12.782% rate from 2019 onward: for individuals earning at or above 120 times the hourly gross SMIC the bonus is capped at 29.101% of the lump sum, while for incomes between 59 and 120 times the hourly gross SMIC the bonus is scaled down proportionally using this same rate in the formula (0.29101*lump sum)*(1-((120*SMIC-income)/(120*SMIC-59*SMIC))).

description.en: The flat monthly housing package (forfait logement) deducted from the Activity Allowance for a single person with no children, expressed as a first-year-average (FYA) value that blends the pre- and post-1 July uprating amounts within the year. It is used in bsawk_fr's BenCalc Comp_perTU parameter to calculate the 'applicable housing package to be deducted' in the benefit formula: Allowance = (lump sum + 59.85%/61% of work income + bonus) − (max(resources, lump sum) + housing package). Per the Country Report (Table 2.31), the housing package equals 12% of the gross activity-allowance lump sum for a single claimant, with the 2025 value being €75.99, matching this constant's latest value.

description.en: This constant is the flat, per-tax-unit (household) amount of the French 'aide exceptionnelle de solidarité' (COVID-19-linked social assistance top-up), simulated by the bsaeccm_fr policy. In the model it feeds the Comp_perTU parameter of bsaeccm_fr's BenCalc function (labelled 'Benefit calculation'), which sums up the components that make up the exceptional payment for each eligible tax/benefit unit, together with the per-child amount ($bsaeccm_child_amt). The EUROMOD country report lists bsaeccm_s as 'Social assistance linked to Covid-19', a scheme that existed only around the pandemic period and is marked as not applicable/not simulated ('-' / n/a) in the 2022-2025 systems, and it is not covered in the current (2025/2026) benefits policy note, which is consistent with the constant's latest value being 'n/a'.

label.en: Tax rates

description.en: This is the tax rate applied to compute the recurrent local property tax on built properties (taxe foncière sur les propriétés bâties, TFPB) in the French EUROMOD spine policy tpr_fr, currently 30.62%. It is used in tpr_fr/BenCalc as the parameter Comp_perTU, i.e. it is multiplied against the taxable base (approximating the cadastral rental value of built real estate) per tax unit to derive the property-tax liability. TFPB rates are in reality set locally by each commune/intercommunality/department and vary widely; the constant represents a single (average/simplified) national rate used by the model since EUROMOD does not have data on local rate variation. No direct confirmation of the exact scheme name was found in the supplied 'taxes' theme note (which covers IRPP, CSG, CRDS and related contributions but not property tax), so the interpretation is based on the constant's name, label ('Tax rates') and usage pattern.

classification.reason: Tax rate set by legislation

It feeds into the same tpr_fr/BenCalc computation (parameter Comp_perTU) that derives the property-tax liability per tax unit. Its current value is 0, meaning the model does not levy any tax on non-built property in the latest system (this component of the property tax is effectively switched off/not simulated), a change from its earlier non-zero setting. As with the built-property rate, no explicit description of this tax was present in the supplied theme note, so the reading relies on the constant's name and its parallel role to $tpr_rate_baties.

label.en: Thresholds for total exemption

description.en: This is the base income threshold used to determine total exemption from the property tax (taxe foncière), calculated for a household with the base number of 'quotient familial' shares/parts. It is used in tpr_fr/ArithOp (parameter Formula), whose function comment states it 'calculates threshold for total exemption with quotient familial' — i.e. it combines with $tpr_threshold2 (the per-additional-part increment) to build a household-specific income ceiling below which the taxpayer is fully exempt from the property tax. This mirrors the real French rule (Article 1417 of the Code Général des Impôts) exempting low-income elderly, disabled or modest-income households from taxe foncière based on their revenu fiscal de référence adjusted for family composition; its current value is €10,708 (annual). This structural detail is not covered in the supplied 'taxes' theme note, so confidence rests on the constant's label, name and the ArithOp function comment.
